query: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) is an unmodified α + β dual-phase alloy whose low hardness and poor friction and wear properties limit its use under extreme-service and high-contact-stress conditions. Formulate one hypothesis for an intervention that could improve its hardness and wear resistance without sacrificing its existing beneficial properties. State the intervention, proposed mechanism, predicted outcome relative to untreated TC4, applicable operating or test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Plasma nitriding the surface of TC4 (Ti6Al4V) will improve its hardness and wear resistance while preserving its bulk ductility and low weight characteristics.
generation.material_initial_state: Unmodified α + β dual-phase TC4 alloy with native surface properties.
generation.intervention: Apply a controlled plasma nitriding process to diffuse nitrogen into the surface of TC4.
generation.conditions: Treatment conducted at optimized temperatures and durations that produce a thin surface layer under high-contact-stress and friction conditions, without altering the substrate microstructure.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a uniform, thin and adherent TiN-rich layer at the alloy surface.
generation.mechanism: Nitrogen diffuses into the surface during plasma nitriding forming hard TiN phases while maintaining the advantageous bulk properties of the TC4 alloy.
generation.predicted_outcome: Plasma nitrided TC4 is expected to exhibit a significant increase in surface hardness and improved wear resistance compared to untreated TC4, while retaining similar ductility and weight characteristics.
generation.baseline: Untreated TC4 alloy characterized by low hardness and suboptimal friction and wear properties under extreme-service conditions.
generation.boundary: The improvement is anticipated only when nitriding parameters (temperature, duration, plasma conditions) are optimized to prevent excessive thickness or structural changes that could induce brittleness.
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of improvement may depend on precise process control, and further experiments are necessary to determine the reproducibility and optimal conditions.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of TC4 samples: one set undergoes the plasma nitriding treatment under the defined optimized conditions and another set remains untreated. Perform surface microhardness testing and standardized pin-on-disk wear tests under high-contact-stress conditions.
measurements: Surface microhardness values (e.g., using Vickers hardness testing) measured across the depth profile.
Wear rate and friction coefficient during pin-on-disk tests.
Microstructural analysis (optical or electron microscopy) to verify formation of a TiN-rich layer and preservation of the underlying microstructure.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the plasma nitrided samples do not demonstrate a statistically significant increase in surface hardness (e.g., a notable percentage increase compared to untreated samples) or fail to show improved wear resistance under high-contact-stress conditions, the hypothesis will be falsified.

drafts.hypothesis: Plasma nitriding of TC4 (Ti6Al4V) will form a thin TiN-rich surface layer that significantly increases hardness and wear resistance while preserving the beneficial bulk ductility and low weight characteristics of the alloy.
drafts.material_initial_state: Unmodified α + β dual-phase TC4 alloy with its native surface properties.
drafts.intervention: Apply a controlled plasma nitriding process to TC4 to diffuse nitrogen into the surface.
drafts.conditions: Treatment performed at temperatures of 700–900°C for durations that yield a surface layer thickness of about a few microns without altering the substrate microstructure; subsequent testing under high-contact-stress and friction conditions at room to moderate temperatures.
drafts.structural_mediator: Formation of a uniform, thin, and adherent TiN or Ti(N) phase layer at the surface.
drafts.mechanism: Nitrogen diffuses into the TC4 alloy surface during plasma nitriding, forming hard TiN phases that increase surface hardness and wear resistance while the underlying α + β phases retain their base mechanical properties.
drafts.predicted_outcome: Treated TC4 will exhibit significantly increased surface hardness (e.g., an increase of 50% or more as compared to untreated material) and improved wear resistance in friction tests, with minimal impact on the alloy’s inherent ductility and other beneficial properties.
drafts.baseline: Untreated TC4 alloy exhibiting low hardness and suboptimal friction and wear properties in extreme-service conditions.
drafts.boundary: Effectiveness is anticipated only when the nitriding treatment parameters (temperature, duration, plasma conditions) are optimized to create a thin surface layer; excessive treatment may lead to undesirable microstructural changes or brittleness.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of TC4 samples: one set undergoes the plasma nitriding treatment under the stated conditions and the other is kept untreated. Conduct microhardness testing (e.g., via Vickers indentation) across the depth profile for both sets and perform standardized pin-on-disk friction and wear tests under high-contact-stress conditions. Compare the hardness and wear metrics of the treated and untreated samples.
measurements: Surface microhardness values (Vickers hardness numbers) at various depths from the surface.
Wear rate (mass or volume loss) and friction coefficient during pin-on-disk tests.
Microstructural characterization (optical or electron microscopy) to confirm formation of the TiN phase and integrity of the underlying material.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the plasma nitriding treated samples do not exhibit a statistically significant increase in surface hardness (e.g., less than a 50% increase over untreated samples) and fail to demonstrate improved wear resistance (comparable or higher wear rates and friction coefficients) under the defined experimental conditions, then the hypothesis that plasma nitriding improves the TC4 alloy's surface properties is falsified.
